places.name: Museo del Prado
places.description: Spain's national art gallery and one of the world's finest collections. Velázquez's Las Meninas, Goya's Black Paintings, Bosch's Garden of Earthly Delights. 8,000 works on permanent display.
highlights: Free 6–8pm daily and all day Sunday

places.name: Mercado de San Miguel
places.description: Art Nouveau iron-and-glass market hall rebuilt 1916, steps from Plaza Mayor. Jamón ibérico, anchovies, tortilla española, craft vermouth. The definitive tapas experience in Madrid.
highlights: Jamón ibérico 5J — best cut in Madrid
Craft vermouth bar with house olives

places.name: Parque del Retiro
places.description: 125 hectares of former royal gardens in the heart of Madrid. Crystal Palace (Palacio de Cristal), rowing lake, Sunday flea market, and the world's only public monument to the Devil (Ángel Caído).
highlights: Ángel Caído — world's only devil monument

places.name: Museo Reina Sofía
places.description: Spain's national museum of modern art in a converted 18th-century hospital. Picasso's Guernica (room 206), Dalí, Miró, Juan Gris. Renzo Piano extension. Free after 7pm Monday to Saturday.
highlights: Dalí and Miró on permanent display

places.name: El Rastro
places.description: Europe's largest outdoor flea market, held every Sunday in La Latina. 3,500 stalls of vintage clothing, prints, antiques, tools, vinyl. Pre-market vermut at Bar Santurce, post-market at El Retiro.
highlights: 3,500 stalls — largest outdoor flea in Europe
Calle Ribera de Curtidores for antiques
Vermouth bars in La Latina after browsing

places.name: Estadio Santiago Bernabéu
places.description: Real Madrid's renovated 81,000-seat cathedral, reopened 2023 with retractable grass pitch and 360° video ring. Museum tour includes 37 Champions League trophies and the original Bernabéu dressing room.
highlights: 37 Champions League trophies in the museum
Tours year-round, match atmosphere on event days

places.name: Gran Vía — Art Deco Walk
places.description: Madrid's grand 1.3km boulevard: Edificio Metropolis (1911), Telefónica Building (1929, Spain's first skyscraper), Callao cinema façades, and neon-signed theatres. Best experienced in the golden hour.

places.name: Chocolatería San Ginés
places.description: Open since 1894, never closed for a single day. Churros con chocolate — thin crispy sticks with thick, dark Spanish drinking chocolate. At its best at 3am, filled with clubbers and early risers equally.
